{{Short description|Statistics regarding ethnicity, religion and language in Luton, Bedfordshire, England}}
{{Use British English|date=March 2019}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2019}}
{{Infobox place demographics|place=[[Luton]]|image_size=350|caption=Population pyramid of Luton|size_of_population=225,261 (2021)|density=4,696/km2 (12,160/sq mi) (2011)|image=File:Luton population pyramid.svg}}[[File:Population Density Luton 2011 census.png|thumb|Population density in the 2011 census in Luton]]
'''[[Luton]]''', [[Bedfordshire]], [[England]] is an ethnically and culturally diverse town of 203,201 people.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.luton.gov.uk/Environment/Lists/LutonDocuments/PDF/Planning/Census/2011%20census%20data/LUTON%20BOROUGH%20PROFILE.pdf|title=LUTON BOROUGH PROFILE 2011 CENSUS DATA}}</ref> It is primarily urban, with a population density of {{convert|4696|PD/sqkm|PD/sqmi|abbr=on}}. Luton has seen several waves of immigration. In the early part of the 20th century, there was immigration of [[Irish people|Irish]] and [[Scottish people|Scottish]] people to the town. These were followed by [[British African-Caribbean community|Afro-Caribbean]] and [[South Asia|Asian]] immigrants. More recently immigrants from other [[European Union]] countries have made Luton their home. As a result of this Luton has a diverse ethnic mix, with a significant population of Asian descent, mainly [[Pakistani people|Pakistani]] 29,353 (14.4%) and [[Bangladeshi people|Bangladeshi]] 13,606 (6.7%).

<ref name="2011census">{{cite web|url=http://www.neighbourhood.statistics.gov.uk/dissemination/LeadTableView.do?a=7&b=6275157&c=luton&d=13&e=62&g=6394327&i=1001x1003x1032x1004&m=0&r=1&s=1361379856428&enc=1&dsFamilyId=2477|title=Local Authority by Ethnic Group|publisher=Office for National Statistics|access-date=20 February 2013}}</ref>

Since the 2011 census, Luton has had a white British population less than 50%, one of three towns in the United Kingdom along with [[Leicester]] and [[Slough]]. Luton has a majority white population, when non-British white people such as the Irish and Eastern Europeans are included.<ref name="2011census" /> Identity wise, 81% of the population of Luton define themselves as British of any race.<ref>{{cite web|last=Philipson |first=Alice |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/immigration/9792392/White-Britons-a-minority-in-Leicester-Luton-and-Slough.html |title=White Britons a minority in Leicester, Luton and Slough |date=10 January 2013 |publisher=Telegraph |access-date=17 March 2013}}</ref>
[[File:Luton's industry sectors over time.svg|thumb|Industry sectors of Luton over time]]

==Ethnicity==
[[File:Luton ethnic demography from 1971 to 2021.gif|thumb|Luton ethnic demography from 1971 to 2021]]
[[File:Population pyramid of Luton by ethnicity in 2021.svg|thumb|Population pyramid of Luton by ethnicity in 2021]]
[[File:Ethnic makeup of Luton by single year ages in 2021.svg|thumb|Ethnic makeup of Luton by single year ages in 2021]]
The following table shows the ethnic group of respondents for estimations for 1971 and in the 1991 to 2021 censuses in Luton.

There was likely 600 to 700 'coloured' people within Luton in 1958, around 300 of these being Afro-Caribbeans, 250 Pakistanis and 60 Indians.<ref name=":4">{{Cite book |last=J. A.G. Griffith |first=Judith Henderson |url=http://archive.org/details/colouredimmigran0000jagg |title=Coloured Immigrants in Britain |date=1960 |publisher=Oxford University Press |others=Internet Archive |page=15}}</ref>

Luton is a majority minority town in which no single ethnic group make up the majority of residents, however by broad multi-ethnic groups, [[White people in the United Kingdom|Whites]] make up 54.7% of the population, a decline of 25.5% from 1991 when Whites made up 4 out of every 5 residents (80.2%). [[British Asian|Asian British]] people have grown in proportional size, having gone from 14% in 1991 to nearly one third of the town's population (30%) in 2011. [[Black British people|Black British]] residents have also increased from nearly 5% to nearly 10% in two decades as well as [[Mixed (United Kingdom ethnicity category)|Mixed]] residents who have gone from 2.6% in 2001 to 4.1% in 2011.

=== Ethnicity of school pupils ===
Luton's schools are [[Majority minority|majority-minority]], that being no single ethnic group makes up the majority, the single largest group is [[British Pakistanis]] at 25.1% of the school pupil population and the largest multi-ethnic group being [[British Asian|Asian British]] people at 47.4% in 2022, which was previous [[White people in the United Kingdom|White's]] at 53.5% in 2004. The white  [[White British]] population has declined from a near majority in 2004 at 49.5% to 17.2% in 2022. [[Black British people|Black British]] people and [[Mixed (United Kingdom ethnicity category)|Mixed people]] have also increased. However, other ethnicities have declined from a peak of 3.7% in 2016 to 2.2% in 2022.
